2015 - 2024 · Staff Technical Writer

Documentation Modernization and Publishing Automation at Synopsys

Led documentation modernization from unstructured FrameMaker to DITA, built CI/CD publishing pipelines with GitHub Actions and Sphinx, and integrated Typesense search to improve discoverability across processor platform documentation.

DITAFrameMakerSphinxGitHub ActionsAWS S3TypesenseCI/CDDocumentation Infrastructure

Problem

Documentation for complex hardware and software processor products was maintained using unstructured FrameMaker, a legacy desktop authoring tool. This created multiple challenges:

  • No content reuse across product lines, leading to duplicated effort and inconsistencies
  • A customer requirement for DITA-formatted source alongside PDF deliverables, with an ongoing two-year commitment for updates
  • Manual publishing workflows that required rebuilding and uploading documentation by hand for each release
  • Default Sphinx search was inadequate for the growing documentation corpus, making it difficult for users to find information

My Role

As a Staff Technical Writer over nearly nine years, I owned documentation delivery for multiple processor platforms, led format modernization initiatives, built publishing automation, and drove documentation infrastructure improvements.

What I Did

DITA Modernization from FrameMaker

  1. Evaluated two approaches for DITA conversion: maintaining FrameMaker as the primary source with per-release DITA exports, or fully converting to DITA as the primary authoring format
  2. Chose full DITA conversion because the internal content reuse requirement made it the stronger long-term approach
  3. Managed the conversion using a third-party migration service (Stilo Migrate) for the initial unstructured-to-DITA conversion, then owned all pre-conversion and post-conversion cleanup
  4. Continued authoring in DITA for all subsequent releases, delivering both DITA source and PDF output to the customer

Publishing Automation with GitHub Actions

  1. Built a CI/CD pipeline using GitHub Actions that automatically generates HTML from reStructuredText documentation using Sphinx and deploys it to AWS S3
  2. Designed the workflow to trigger on pull request merges and also support manual dispatch for ad-hoc publishing
  3. Configured artifact archiving so each build produces a downloadable documentation snapshot alongside the live deployment
  4. Documented the entire pipeline so non-technical team members could understand, maintain, and extend it

Search Integration with Typesense

  1. Replaced the default Sphinx search with Typesense, a fast, typo-tolerant search engine
  2. Configured the Docsearch Scraper to crawl the documentation site and index content with proper heading hierarchy
  3. Integrated the search bar into the ReadTheDocs theme using custom JavaScript and CSS injection
  4. Improved search relevance by tuning selectors to match the documentation theme structure

Documentation Site UX Improvements

  • Designed a documentation homepage template using Sphinx-design extension (cards, tabs, grids) for improved discoverability
  • Added custom navigation menus to the ReadTheDocs theme header using JavaScript injection for cross-product navigation
  • Implemented Perforce changelist templates to improve documentation change traceability

Constraints

  • Nine years of accumulated legacy content across multiple processor product lines
  • Distributed engineering teams across multiple geographies and time zones
  • Customer contractual requirement for ongoing DITA deliverables (not a one-time conversion)
  • Limited IT support for infrastructure changes (for example, Perforce trigger restrictions that required client-side workarounds)

Outcomes

Customer Impact

  • Delivered DITA source and PDF documentation to a key customer over multiple release cycles, meeting contractual requirements
  • Improved search experience with Typesense integration, replacing inadequate default Sphinx search
  • Better content organization through homepage redesign and cross-product navigation

Operational Impact

  • Automated publishing reduced manual build-and-upload effort to a single pull request merge
  • Enabled content reuse across product lines through DITA conversion, reducing duplicate authoring
  • Improved documentation change traceability through customized Perforce changelist templates
  • Conducted documentation quality audits that improved consistency across all product documentation

Technical Writing and Infrastructure Overlap

This work demonstrates a pattern that recurred throughout my Synopsys tenure: documentation professionals can own significant infrastructure improvements (CI/CD, search, hosting, format migration) without needing dedicated engineering resources, if they are willing to learn the tooling and treat documentation as a product with its own build, deploy, and operations lifecycle.

Lessons Learned

  • Full DITA conversion is the right choice when content reuse is the primary driver; per-release exports are better when the conversion is purely a customer deliverable format
  • Publishing automation pays for itself within one release cycle; manual publishing is the single largest source of preventable documentation errors
  • Owning infrastructure (CI/CD, search integration) gives documentation teams independence and speed; waiting for IT or engineering support creates bottlenecks
  • Search quality is a documentation UX feature, not just a platform feature; investing in Typesense integration had measurable impact on user satisfaction
